- **Member Onboarding** – no documented pathway from signup → first class → habit formation (risk: inconsistent experience, high early churn)
- **Churn & Cancellation** – no win-back playbook or exit interview protocol (money left on table)

- **Class Quality Audit** – no standardised observation/feedback loop (quality drift undetected)

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist**
Pull your last 3 months of booking data. Which classes/services actually get booked? Which sit empty? Build your menu around *what sells*, not what you think should sell. This kills decision paralysis and keeps it simple.

**Create TWO separate documents (not one combined menu)**
- **Coach version**: Service codes, pricing tiers, what's included/excluded, upsell triggers (e.g., "1:1 sessions trigger here if client mentions X")
- **Member version**: Clean, benefit-focused (not feature-focused). Replace "60-min class" with "Full-body strength session — build muscle and confidence"

**Embed pricing psychology into the structure**
Use a 3-tier approach for each service (good/better/best). This makes mid-tier feel safer and often captures people who'd otherwise pick the cheapest option. Example: Class packages at 4-class, 8-class, unlimited.

**Get coaches to test-drive it tomorrow**
Don't wait for perfection. Give coaches draft menus Friday, ask them Friday evening: "What confused you? What would you sell harder?" Iterate by Monday. Real usage beats guesswork.

**Version it for your channels immediately**
Make it real: print small physical menus for your gym floor, create a simple PDF for WhatsApp/email, and update your Instagram bio link same day. Inconsistency kills conversions.

## REVENUE TRENDS & ALERTS

**What's off-track:**
- **Revenue per member collapsed from £145 (July) → £103 (Oct).** You're adding members (120→173) but revenue/head is down 29% in 3 months. This is your biggest red flag.
- **Last 3 months avg £17,320 vs prior 3 months avg £17,668.** Flat-to-declining despite 30 more members. The studio expansion isn't yet translating to revenue lift.
- **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** (relocation month — understandable) but you're still at 3.9–6.2%, which is acceptable. That's not the problem.

**The problem is pricing or membership mix:**
- Either new members are on cheaper tiers, or existing members aren't upgrading to classes/PT/merchandise.
- **Action 1: Audit your membership tiers.** What % are on the base tier vs premium (classes + PT credits + retail)? Target: shift 15% of base-tier members to premium within 60 days. Premium should carry at least 40% margin lift vs entry tier. Use email + 1-to-1 outreach.
- **Action 2: Introduce a class pass upsell.** New 10-class bundles (no membership) at £89–99. Retention is only good if members *use* the studio. Quiet class slots (early morning, late evening, mid-week) should have a "fill-the-class" discount: existing members + 3 friends for £25/head. Track attendance by time; move weak classes.
- **Action 3: Launch a PT/nutrition membership add-on.** Even 10% uptake at +£25/month per member = +£400/month (at 162 members). Personal training and body comp tracking are high-margin, and women-only is a selling point.
